newsitem.title: UK: GDR Report-India rests after UK holiday.
newsitem.headline: GDR Report-India rests after UK holiday.

text.p: Trading in Indian global depositary receipts was subdued after a market holiday here on Monday and the absence of any firm direction from Bombay.
It has been a relatively quiet day, said a broker.
The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and other regional bourses will be shut for a Hindu festival on Wednesday but the National Stock Exchange (NSE) will be open.
The BSE 30-share index closed 5.25 points higher at 3438.80.
Gujarat Ambuja Cements, which reported a 47 percent rise in 1995/96 net profit to 1.48 billion rupees, closed little changed at $8.50/$9.25.

"That is the problem. We have had good earnings and the stocks have not moved, and with the talk in India that earnings for the current half are not going to be as good as last year, there is clearly room for a decline in sentiment," said the broker.
Closing prices for the HSBC James Capel Indian GDR Index JCEAI were unavailable because of price feed problems from stocks on the London Stock Exchanges SEAQ International system.
The Korea Composite Index fell 5.14 points to provisionally close at 761.75 after nine businessmen were found guilty of bribery by the Seoul District Criminal Court on Monday.

The Taiwan Weighted Index Taiwan rose 32.05 points or 0.52 percent at 6,232.53 on hopes its forthcoming addition to the MSCI index would lead to a flow of foreign funds. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
